Bless your heart. ACA subsidies are not a “bonus program” and they are not Covid payments. They are tax credits that reduce the cost of health insurance premiums for people who buy insurance on the marketplace. They work the same way a normal tax deduction or credit works: your income determines how much assistance you qualify for. The government doesn’t just hand out money to insurance companies. It caps how much a person has to pay for coverage and the tax credit makes up the difference. That is not a bonus, it is a cost-sharing structure written into the law since 2014.

The only thing Biden did was temporarily expand who qualifies so that middle-class families aren’t stuck paying full price if their premiums skyrocket. That expansion had nothing to do with Covid. It was done because health insurance costs are extremely high, and without subsidies, large numbers of Americans would lose coverage. Extending that policy post-Covid doesn’t make it a Covid program any more than Social Security becomes a “pandemic handout” if it continues after a crisis.

And your claim about “waste, fraud, and abuse” sounds dramatic, but ACA subsidies aren’t checks being given away blindly. They are income-verified tax credits that are reconciled at the end of the year. If someone claims more subsidy than they qualify for, they owe it back. Fraud is literally corrected by the IRS at tax time.

So no, Democrats aren’t sending $100 billion to insurance companies. They are making sure working families don’t get priced out of health coverage. Calling that a Covid “bonus” might make for a good slogan, but it has nothing to do with how the law actually works.
